meta.title: ProGramerly - Basic Coding Software for All
meta.author: Johan Wilhelm van Antwerp

full.label: Full Stack
full.desc: Everything. Every app, every runtime, every SDK, every shell. ~45-70 GB, 60-120 min.

ai.label: AI Dev
ai.desc: Claude, MCP servers, local models, Node, Python, Git, VS Code. ~12-20 GB.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.desc: Git, Node, Python, VS Code, Chrome, PowerShell. ~4-8 GB.

items.name: winget (Windows Package Manager)
items.desc: Verifies winget is present; repairs the App Installer source if broken.

items.name: Chocolatey
items.desc: Fallback package engine for anything winget cannot resolve.

steps.cmd: if (-not (Get-Command choco -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; [System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = 3072; iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1')) } else { choco --version }

items.name: Homebrew
items.desc: The macOS package engine. Installed non-interactively if missing.

items.name: Xcode Command Line Tools
items.desc: Apple's compiler toolchain. Required by Homebrew and most native builds.

items.name: Git
items.desc: Distributed version control. On Windows this also brings Git Bash.

items.name: GitHub CLI
items.desc: gh - clone, PR, release and auth from the terminal.

items.name: GitHub Desktop
items.desc: Graphical Git client.

items.name: Git LFS
items.desc: Large file storage for binary assets.

items.name: PowerShell 7+
items.desc: Cross-platform PowerShell (pwsh). Sits alongside Windows PowerShell 5.1.

items.name: Windows Terminal
items.desc: Tabbed terminal host for cmd, PowerShell, WSL and Git Bash.

items.name: OpenSSH (client + agent)
items.desc: The ssh client, ssh-keygen and ssh-add, plus the ssh-agent service enabled so a passphrase-protected key is typed once per boot instead of once per push.

steps.cmd: $c = Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name 'OpenSSH.Client*' | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'Installed' }; if ($c) { Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name $c.Name | Out-Null }; (Get-Command ssh -ErrorAction Stop).Source
Set-Service ssh-agent -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service ssh-agent; Write-Output "ssh-agent: $((Get-Service ssh-agent).Status)"

items.name: Nushell
items.desc: Structured-data shell. Good for pipelines that carry tables, not text.

items.name: Oh My Posh
items.desc: Prompt theme engine for every shell.

items.name: Starship prompt
items.desc: Minimal, fast, cross-shell prompt.

items.name: Update all shells & package sources
items.desc: winget source update + choco upgrade all / brew update && brew upgrade.

items.name: Node.js (LTS + Latest via fnm)
items.desc: fnm version manager, then Node LTS and Node Latest, LTS set as default.

post.cmd: eval "$(fnm env)" && fnm install --lts && fnm install latest && fnm default lts-latest

items.name: Node.js LTS (system install)
items.desc: A plain system Node so global CLIs work even before fnm is on PATH.

items.name: pnpm, Yarn, npm-check-updates
items.desc: The other JS package managers plus a dependency upgrader.

items.name: Electron + Electron Builder + Forge
items.desc: Desktop app stack (this installer is built on it).

items.name: TypeScript + tsx + ESLint + Prettier
items.desc: The standard TS toolchain, installed globally.

items.name: Python 3 (latest + 3.12)
items.desc: Latest CPython plus 3.12 for compatibility, with py launcher on Windows.

post.winCmd: py -3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
post.cmd: python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
python3 -m pip install --upgrade --break-system-packages pip setuptools wheel

items.name: uv, pipx, poetry, ruff
items.desc: Modern Python packaging and lint stack.

post.cmd: py -3 -m pip install --user pipx poetry ruff

items.name: .NET SDK (all supported LTS + current)
items.desc: .NET 10, 9 and 8 SDKs side by side, plus the ASP.NET runtimes.

items.name: .NET Framework 4.8 Dev Pack
items.desc: Legacy Framework targeting pack for older Windows projects.

items.name: Java JDK (Temurin 21 LTS + 17 LTS)
items.desc: Eclipse Temurin OpenJDK builds.

items.name: Go
items.desc: The Go toolchain.

items.name: Rust (rustup)
items.desc: rustup, cargo and the stable toolchain.

items.name: C/C++ toolchain (LLVM, CMake, Ninja)
items.desc: Clang/LLVM, CMake and Ninja. MSVC comes with Visual Studio.

items.name: Ruby & PHP
items.desc: Rounds out the mainstream scripting languages.

items.name: Visual Studio Code
items.desc: The editor. Extensions are installed in a follow-up step.

items.name: VS Code extension pack (critical set)
items.desc: Every language server, debugger, database client, cloud tool and AI assistant a mixed stack needs - 57 extensions, installed with --force so a re-run repairs a broken one.

items.name: Visual Studio Community
items.desc: Full IDE with .NET desktop, ASP.NET, C++ desktop, Node.js and Azure workloads. Large download (~15-30 GB).

items.name: Visual Studio Build Tools
items.desc: MSVC compiler + Windows SDK without the full IDE. Needed by node-gyp and native npm modules.

items.name: Android Studio + Android SDK
items.desc: Android IDE, SDK, platform tools and emulator.

items.name: Claude Desktop
items.desc: Anthropic's desktop client. MCP servers configure into this.

items.name: Google Chrome
items.desc: Browser. Also the host for the Claude in Chrome extension.

items.name: OBS Studio
items.desc: Screen recording and streaming.

items.name: Canva
items.desc: Design app.

items.name: Obsidian
items.desc: Local-first markdown knowledge base.

items.name: Notion
items.desc: Workspace and docs.

items.name: Miro (MIRA)
items.desc: Collaborative whiteboard desktop client.

items.name: Docker Desktop
items.desc: Containers. Several MCP servers ship as container images.

items.name: 7-Zip / Keka
items.desc: Archive tool.

items.name: Claude Code CLI
items.desc: Anthropic's agentic coding CLI.

items.name: Qwen Code CLI
items.desc: Alibaba's open-source terminal coding agent (Qwen3-Coder).

items.name: Gemini CLI + OpenAI Codex CLI
items.desc: The other two mainstream terminal agents.

items.name: Ollama
items.desc: Run open models locally. Qwen, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek.

items.name: Pull starter models (coder, chat, reasoning, embeddings, vision)
items.desc: qwen2.5-coder for code, llama3.2 for chat, deepseek-r1 for reasoning, nomic-embed-text for embeddings and llava for vision. Roughly 12 GB.

items.name: LM Studio
items.desc: GUI for running and serving local models (the closest thing to a 'Qwen Studio').

items.name: MCP runtime prerequisites
items.desc: uvx and npx must be on PATH for MCP servers to launch.

items.name: MCP servers (filesystem, memory, git, fetch, time, sqlite, playwright, sequential-thinking)
items.desc: Pre-caches the reference MCP servers so Claude Desktop launches them instantly.

items.name: Write claude_desktop_config.json
items.desc: Merges the installed MCP servers into Claude Desktop's config. Existing entries are preserved; a .bak is written first.

items.name: Azure CLI, AWS CLI, Google Cloud CLI
items.desc: The three cloud command lines.

items.name: Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)
items.desc: Python agent framework: pip install google-adk.

items.name: AI SDKs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google GenAI)
items.desc: Python and Node SDKs for the major model providers.

steps.cmd: py -3 -m pip install --user anthropic openai google-genai mcp
steps.macCmd: python3 -m pip install --user anthropic openai google-genai mcp --break-system-packages

items.name: Windows SDK
items.desc: Headers, libs and tools for native Windows development.

items.name: CLI toolbelt (jq, ripgrep, fzf, curl, wget, fd, bat, delta)
items.desc: The utilities every other script assumes you have.

items.name: Build libraries (OpenSSL, pkg-config, libffi, protobuf)
items.desc: Native dependencies most language ecosystems link against.

items.name: Cascadia Code + JetBrains Mono Nerd Font
items.desc: Terminal fonts with the glyphs Oh My Posh and Starship expect.

items.name: WSL 2 + Ubuntu
items.desc: Windows Subsystem for Linux with the Ubuntu distro. Needs a reboot to finish.

items.name: archify (AntwerpDesignsIonity)
items.desc: Clones github.com/AntwerpDesignsIonity/archify into your dev root. Private repo - needs gh auth login first.

items.name: Ionity brand assets
items.desc: Clones github.com/AntwerpDesignsIonity/ionity-assets1 for logos, icons and Policy 986 AED documents.

items.name: Create Ionity dev workspace
items.desc: Creates the standard folder tree and drops a Policy 986 AED README at the dev root.

items.name: Cursor
items.desc: AI-native fork of VS Code.

items.name: Windsurf
items.desc: Codeium's agentic editor.

items.name: Zed
items.desc: Rust-built editor, very fast, good multiplayer.

items.name: JetBrains Toolbox
items.desc: One launcher for IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion, Android Studio.

items.name: Neovim
items.desc: Modal editor for the terminal.

items.name: Edge Dev + Firefox Developer Edition
items.desc: The other two engines, so a site can be tested where it actually breaks.

items.name: Chrome extensions (uBlock Origin Lite + Claude)
items.desc: Ad and tracker blocking plus Claude in Chrome. On Windows with administrator rights both are added to Chrome's force-install policy list; otherwise the Web Store pages open so you can add them with one click.

items.name: OpenCode
items.desc: Terminal coding agent, provider agnostic.

items.name: Aider
items.desc: Pair programming in the terminal against your git history.

items.name: More agent CLIs (Cline, Goose, Continue, Aichat)
items.desc: A second bench of terminal agents so you are never stuck on one vendor.

items.name: Managed Python environment (.venvs/ionity)
items.desc: One virtual environment every AI and data item below installs into, at Development/.venvs/ionity. Nothing lands in the system Python.

items.name: PyTorch (torch, torchvision, torchaudio)
items.desc: CPU wheels by default - they work on every machine. Swap in a CUDA or ROCm index later if you have the hardware.

items.name: Hugging Face stack (transformers, datasets, accelerate)
items.desc: transformers, datasets, accelerate, tokenizers, safetensors, sentence-transformers and the huggingface CLI.

items.name: TensorFlow + Keras
items.desc: TensorFlow with Keras 3 and TensorBoard.

items.name: Data science toolkit (numpy, pandas, sklearn, Jupyter)
items.desc: numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, JupyterLab, ipykernel, OpenCV, Pillow.

items.name: Agent frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI)
items.desc: The orchestration layer plus the Anthropic, OpenAI and Google SDKs, inside the managed venv.

items.name: SQLite + DB Browser
items.desc: The engine, the CLI and a GUI that opens a .db file without ceremony.

items.name: MongoDB Community + Compass + mongosh
items.desc: Server, shell, database tools and the Compass GUI.

items.name: PostgreSQL + pgAdmin
items.desc: PostgreSQL server, client tools and the pgAdmin console.

items.name: MySQL + Workbench
items.desc: MySQL Community Server and MySQL Workbench.

items.name: SQL Server Express + SSMS + Azure Data Studio
items.desc: Microsoft's stack: the Express engine, Management Studio and Azure Data Studio.

items.name: Redis + DBeaver universal client
items.desc: DBeaver talks to every engine above. Redis runs natively on macOS; on Windows it lives in WSL or Docker, and RedisInsight is the console for it.

items.name: XAMPP (Apache + MariaDB + PHP + Perl)
items.desc: The classic local LAMP stack in one installer.

items.name: PHP + Composer + Laravel + Symfony
items.desc: PHP CLI, Composer, the Laravel installer and the Symfony CLI.

items.name: Ruby on Rails
items.desc: Rails, Bundler and the Rails command line, on top of the Ruby runtime.

items.name: Django + DRF + PostgreSQL/MySQL drivers
items.desc: Django, Django REST Framework, Celery, Gunicorn and the drivers for both PostgreSQL and MySQL, in the managed venv.

items.name: React, Express, Vite, Nest, PM2
items.desc: The JavaScript side: Vite and create-vite for React, the Express generator, NestJS CLI, nodemon, PM2, serve and concurrently.

items.name: MERN starter project
items.desc: Writes a working React + Express + MongoDB starter into Development/Sandbox/mern-starter - server, client, scripts and a README - ready to npm install and run.

items.name: .NET web tooling (EF Core, ASP.NET, Azure Functions)
items.desc: dotnet-ef, the ASP.NET scaffolder, the user-secrets tool and the Azure Functions Core Tools.

items.name: Flutter + Dart SDK
items.desc: The Flutter SDK and the Dart toolchain.

items.name: Kotlin + Gradle + Maven
items.desc: The Kotlin compiler and the two JVM build systems everything Android leans on.

items.name: Android SDK command line tools + platform tools
items.desc: sdkmanager, adb and fastboot without opening Android Studio, plus a licence acceptance pass.

steps.winCmd: if (Get-Command sdkmanager -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { cmd /c "echo y| sdkmanager --licenses" }

items.name: React Native + Expo
items.desc: The Expo tooling, EAS CLI and the React Native community CLI.

items.name: Arduino IDE 2 + arduino-cli
items.desc: The IDE and the command line compiler/uploader that CI can drive.

items.name: PlatformIO Core + IDE extension
items.desc: PlatformIO in the managed venv, the VS Code extension, and udev/driver setup where it applies. This is the best embedded IDE going.

items.name: ESP-IDF tooling, esptool, MicroPython, Thonny
items.desc: esptool, mpremote, adafruit-ampy and the Thonny editor, plus the ESP-IDF VS Code extension.

items.name: Postman + Insomnia
items.desc: Two API consoles - Postman for collections and teams, Insomnia when you want something lighter.

items.name: HTTPie, Newman, OpenAPI tooling
items.desc: Newman for Postman collections in CI, Redocly and swagger tooling for specs, HTTPie for one-liners.

items.name: Serverless CLIs (AWS SAM, Azure Functions, Firebase, Wrangler)
items.desc: AWS Lambda through SAM, Azure Functions Core Tools, Google Firebase, Cloudflare Workers via Wrangler, plus Vercel and Netlify.

items.name: Cloudflare WARP + cloudflared
items.desc: The Cloudflare desktop client and the tunnel daemon.

items.name: OpenRGB
items.desc: Vendor-neutral RGB control: motherboard 12V and 5V ARGB headers, GPU, RAM, AIO, fans. ProGramerly's Hardware tab talks to its SDK server.

items.name: FanControl
items.desc: Fan curves for every header, GPU and pump. Ships the signed kernel driver that makes writing to the EC possible.

items.name: LibreHardwareMonitor
items.desc: Temperatures, fan RPM, voltages and power straight off the chips. The sensor source for ProGramerly's Hardware tab.

items.name: curl
items.desc: The transfer tool every install script assumes. Windows ships an older curl.exe; this puts the current one on PATH. Homebrew curl on macOS.

items.name: Google Antigravity IDE
items.desc: Google's agent-first IDE - agents across workspaces, VS Code-familiar editing. winget Google.AntigravityIDE; Homebrew cask antigravity.

items.name: Google Antigravity CLI (agy)
items.desc: The Antigravity agent harness in the terminal. Installed with Google's own script: curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.cmd, run, delete. Binary is `agy`; run it once to sign in.

items.name: Antigravity auto-accept (Ionity)
items.desc: Clones github.com/Ionity-Global-Pty-Ltd/antigravity-auto-accept into your dev root - Ionity's utility that accepts Antigravity agent steps without a click each time.
